prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity landscape desktop web product decision comp, approximately 1440×1000, first viewport only
Primary request: Design CareCommand AI’s “Today” workspace option “Shift Timeline” for a busy multi-clinic healthcare practice. The dominant visual move is a large time-led operational now-line across the working day, not a dashboard-card collage. It must instantly show what is happening, what is blocked, who owns it, and what action comes next.
Input image: the supplied current Front Desk screenshot is a visual identity reference only. Preserve its CareCommand chrome, calm navy/indigo clinical identity, Inter-like typography, restrained pale surfaces, compact familiar healthcare controls, semantic status chips, and thin borders. Do not reuse its content, long stacked layout, or sparse right-side whitespace.
Composition/framing:
- Full 1440×1000 desktop application viewport, orthographic straight-on UI screenshot, crisp professional SaaS fidelity, no device frame.
- Persistent slim dark-navy left sidebar with CareCommand AI logo and navigation: Today selected, Patients, Schedule, Work Queue, Communications, Revenue Operations, Connected Care, Insights, Administration.
- Persistent top scope bar with “Bright Health LLC”, clearly marked “SYNTHETIC PILOT TENANT”, Network / 3 clinics, America/New_York, Tue 01 Sep 2026, current time 10:42 AM, and freshness “Refreshed 10:42 · synthetic workspace”.
- Main title “Today” with subtitle “One operating view for the shift”. Compact controls: Network, All clinics, Timeline selected / Queue, Density, and “Open buyer-safe proof” as a secondary shield action.
- The center of the viewport is one large continuous shift timeline from 8:00 AM to 2:00 PM with five aligned swimlanes: Appointments, Calls, Intake, Staff coverage, Follow-ups. A decisive indigo vertical NOW line at 10:42 crosses every lane, with a clear “NOW 10:42” marker. Use subtle hour grid lines and clinic-colored lane markers; keep the rest calm and readable.
- Populate the timeline with realistic operational blocks and concise labels. Appointments include “Ava Rivera · New patient consult”, “Leo Martin · Follow-up”, and “Dr Maya Chen · Downtown”; Calls include “Inbound answered”, “Human handoff”, and “Voicemail follow-up”; Intake includes “Ready”, “Missing signature”, and “Review due”; Staff coverage includes “Jordan Lee · Front desk”, “Nia Patel · Practice manager”, and “Coverage gap 12:00–12:30”; Follow-ups include “Confirm reschedule”, “Consent evidence unknown · Blocked”, and “Call back before 12:15”.
- Attach exceptions and handoffs directly to the precise moments they affect using compact anchored callouts, not floating generic cards. Each expanded exception must visibly show synthetic patient/clinic, owner, SLA age, status/freshness, and one next-action control. Include: “Missing signature” for Ava Rivera at Northside, owner Nia Patel, SLA 18m, Needs attention, action “Open intake”; “Human handoff” for Leo Martin at Midtown, owner Jordan Lee, SLA 4m, action “Join call”; “Provider delayed 20m” at Downtown, four appointments affected, action “Notify affected patients”; and “Consent evidence unknown” with status Blocked and action “Review consent”.
- Progressive disclosure for density: three clinic chips (Downtown, Midtown, Northside), “Showing 18 of 43 events”, compact collapsed-event stacks, a “Show low-risk activity” control, and a narrow right-side “Needs attention now” rail listing the same four exceptions in priority order without duplicating all details.
- Add a small secondary, PHI-safe pathway near the lower right: shield icon plus “Buyer-safe proof”, “Synthetic operational evidence only”, “No live integration or commercial outcome claims”, and action “View evidence timeline”. This must be clearly secondary to live operations.
Visual language:
- CareCommand navy #12142E, brand indigo #4F46E5, white and pale blue-gray #F4F6F9 / #F8FAFC, charcoal text #111827, readable secondary text #4B5563, thin borders #E5EAF0.
- Semantic statuses use muted emerald, amber, red, blue, and violet with both icon/text and color.
- Crisp Inter-style type, tabular numerals, strong hierarchy, generous breathing room around the timeline, compact but readable 12–14px operational details, 22–28px page title.
- Modern enterprise clinical operations aesthetic: mature, precise, calm, highly legible, restrained depth, subtle soft shadows with offsets, no decorative glass, no glossy gradients, no neon, no oversized hero metric, no progress rings, no generic icon-tile cards.
Truth and safety constraints:
- All people and operational data are synthetic and visibly labeled synthetic.
- No diagnosis, treatment, clinical recommendation, PHI, testimonial, customer quote, revenue promise, ROI claim, commercial outcome, or live integration claim.
- Do not imply integrations are live. Do not use real company logos except CareCommand AI.
- Maintain familiar accessible healthcare controls, visible focus states, non-color-only statuses, and exact spellings for the major labels.
- Full-fidelity polished UI, not a wireframe, not a poster, not a marketing landing page.

reference.role: identity reference only: chrome, palette, typography, control character and status language
